newsitem.title: UK: UK Ford workers hold protest meetings on job cuts.
newsitem.headline: UK Ford workers hold protest meetings on job cuts.

text.p: Ford car workers in Britain started a series of mass meetings on Monday to discuss possible action in protest at plans to cut 1,300 jobs at a plant in Liverpool.
Union leaders said workers at the U.S. car giant's 20 British plants would hold consultative meetings over the next three days. The Unions will meet Ford management on Thursday.
A Transport and General Workers Union spokesman told Reuters a decision on whether or not to hold a strike ballot was not expected until after the Thursday meeting.
Under tough trade union laws passed in the 1980s, it could take two to three weeks to collate the results of a secret ballot needed to sanction a strike or other industrial action.

Ford shocked its workforce last week by announcing 1,300 job losses out of a workforce of 4,500 at the Halewood plant in Liverpool, northwest England, which produces Escort cars for the domestic market.
It is expected to concentrate production of the next Escort model in Germany or Spain.
The job cuts placed the future of the Halewood plant in doubt. Ford on Monday confirmed press reports that it had asked for British government aid to maintain production there after the year 2000.
Ford has indicated it would consider building an unspecified new vehicle at Halewood after 2000 subject to improved productivity and job flexibility.
A Ford spokeswoman said the company had raised the issue of aid under the government's regional assistance scheme at a meeting last week with Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang.
"We believe the request is under consideration," a spokeswoman said. She did not put a figure on the request.
